 When will it rain in the DC area again?
 Probably not for a while.
 By 
 Dan Stillman

 Probably not for a while.
 All the major weather models show no precipitation anywhere close to the DC area through at least the end of the month, thanks to high pressure remaining locked in place most of the time. Of course, forecast confidence always drops some once you get more than 7 to 10 days out. (In other words, don't guarantee your kids a dry Halloween just yet.)
 To illustrate the expected dryness, here are total precipitation forecasts from the European and American models through Oct. 31.
 European model forecast of total precipitation (in inches) through Oct. 31. (Pivotal Weather) American (GFS) model forecast of total precipitation (in inches) through Oct. 31. (Pivotal Weather) Other primary models including those operated by Canada and the United Kingdom, as well as several AI models, all show a similar absence of precipitation.
 We called for a "potentially drier finish" to the month in our October outlook , and that does indeed look to be coming to fruition.
 With just 2.08 inches of rain so far this month, compared with the monthly average of 2.50 inches, October appears likely to finish drier than normal. If it does, that would make seven of the first 10 months of 2026 with below-average precipitation.
